title: 1962 AHSME Problem 20
statement: The angles of a pentagon are in arithmetic progression. One of the angles, in degrees, must be:

solutions.text:
The average of the five angles is \(\frac{540^\circ}{5}=108^\circ.\) For five terms in arithmetic progression, the middle term equals the average, so one angle must be \(108^\circ.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Five terms in arithmetic progression have their middle term equal to their average
The interior angles of a pentagon sum to \(540^\circ\)
